label: ex:nitrogen-14-threading
title: The ${}^{14}\mathrm{N}$ maximal braid shortcut vs ${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$ broken alternation
html:
Both {}^{14}\mathrm{N} and {}^{14}\mathrm{C} possess mass number A = 14 and share the braid word skeleton (\sigma_1 \cdots \sigma_{13})^2 (26 crossings). They differ exclusively in crossing chirality assignment: which crossings are same-species (weight q or q^{-1}) and which are mixed (weight (q + q^{-1})/2).

Crossing comparison.

\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{thr}}(7,7) \mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{thr}}(6,8)
Mixed crossings 26 (all) 22
Same-species 0 4 (\mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n})
Coulomb excess 0 -2(q - q^{-1})
Pauli cost 0 (n-p)^2/(4A) asymmetry

Ground-state character of \mathcal{N}(7,7). For p = n = 7, every crossing is a \mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{n} mixed crossing. The mixed crossing weight (q + q^{-1})/2 \approx 1.005 averages the positive weight q = q_0 and the negative weight q^{-1} = 0.901. No crossing incurs the Coulomb penalty (q - q^{-1})/2 \approx 0.105, and none carries the attractive excess -(q - q^{-1})/2.

This constitutes the maximal braid shortcut: all 26 crossings contribute identically. The alternation prevents any generator from appearing twice consecutively, so the Hecke reduction encounters no \sigma_i^2 terms. This renders the Gröbner--Shirshov normal form maximally efficient.

Instability of \mathcal{N}(6,8). For p = 6 and n = 8, the 8 neutrons generate 4 \mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n} crossings (e.g., between neutrons 7–8, 7–9) that break alternation. These same-species crossings carry weight q^{-1} rather than (q + q^{-1})/2, introducing three penalties:

  1. Coulomb deficit: The 4 same-species crossings lack the electromagnetic contribution (q - q^{-1})/2, creating a net Coulomb excess of -2(q - q^{-1}) \approx -0.42 in Skein weight.
  2. Pauli asymmetry cost: The (n - p)^2 / (4A) = 4/56 asymmetry penalty from the Skein binding Lagrangian (Skein binding Lagrangian) contributes an antisymmetric product cost in the categorical action's matter sector.
  3. Hecke reduction cost: The same-species crossings produce \sigma_i^2 terms. Resolving these via the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 increases the total energy.

The fractional ideal volume at the converting generator (generator volume decomposition) evaluates to e(I)/e(R) = 0.1563. This matches the observed Q-value of 0.156 MeV (hadron half-life verification).

The transition {}^{14}\mathrm{C} \to {}^{14}\mathrm{N}. Beta decay converts one neutron to a proton, substituting 4 mixed crossings for 4 same-species crossings. The braid word transforms from a broken alternation into perfect alternation (the maximal shortcut).

Within the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, this transition:

  • Eliminates 4 Hecke reduction steps (\sigma_i^2 resolutions).
  • Lowers the total energy by \Delta E = -3.361 Skein weight units.
  • Releases the Pauli asymmetry cost and Coulomb deficit as the decay Q-value.

The half-life of 5730 years reflects the n = 8 shell structure stabilizing the broken-alternation configuration (shell-structure worked examples).
